purpose: Verify that the multi-reader statistics pipeline runs correctly. NOT an estimate of agreement between people.
decision: The requester decided not to collect a second independent human reader for split H. The v2 hypothesis (that one primary mode by symptom order makes readers agree) is therefore left UNTESTED, not answered with simulated data.
source: Derived from the confirmed human H_r1 workbook by deterministic perturbation. Every simulated reader is statistically dependent on H_r1 by construction.
pipeline_bug_found: Rows where either reader answered 不确定 were silently dropped from the binary Fleiss kappa. With that denominator, every variant scored 1.000 regardless of perturbation. Fixed: 不确定 is now a third category; the older flattering denominator is kept only as an explicitly labelled comparison figure.
why_this_cannot_be_quoted_as_agreement: The number moves from 0.221 to 1.000 purely by turning a parameter in the generator. A statistic that can be dialled to any value proves nothing about people.
The simulated reader is derived from H_r1, so the two are not independent by construction.

check_labeling_independence.py returned NO_RED_FLAG for two of the three variants. That result does NOT certify independence or humanness; it only means the paraphrase signature was absent. The tool can falsify independence, never prove it.
what_is_now_verified: The scorer computes Cohen's kappa for pairs, Fleiss kappa for both the binary and primary-mode layers, handles 不确定 as a third category, reports two denominators instead of picking one, and emits a per-row disagreement table. A real independent workbook could be scored without further code changes.
what_remains_unverified: Whether two independent people agree more under v2 than under v1. No reader-to-reader kappa from real people exists under v2. Split G's four readers (Fleiss kappa 0.922 binary) remain the only multi-person data in this repository.
